claim: Pembrolizumab-based immunotherapy has significantly improved lung cancer patient survival.
source: Although Pembrolizumab-based immunotherapy has significantly improved lung cancer patient survival, many patients show variable efficacy and resistance development.
evidence: This is a general statement about clinical outcomes that is presented as established fact in the introduction.

claim: Many lung cancer patients show variable efficacy and resistance development to Pembrolizumab-based immunotherapy.
source: Although Pembrolizumab-based immunotherapy has significantly improved lung cancer patient survival, many patients show variable efficacy and resistance development.
evidence: This is stated as a known clinical observation in the abstract.

claim: Functional heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment is crucial to modulating drug resistance.
source: Functional heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial to modulating drug resistance; understanding of individual patients' TME that impacts drug response is hampered by lack of appropriate models.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Understanding of individual patients' TME that impacts drug response is hampered by lack of appropriate models.
source: Functional heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial to modulating drug resistance; understanding of individual patients' TME that impacts drug response is hampered by lack of appropriate models.
evidence: This is presented as a rationale for the study approach.

claim: Primary and BM PD-1+ lung cancer OTC responded to Pembrolizumab and Pembrolizumab + WGP treatments, respectively.
source: Primary and BM PD-1+ lung cancer OTC responded to Pembrolizumab and Pembrolizumab + WGP treatments, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Pembrolizumab activated innate immune metabolism and functions in primary OTC.
source: Pembrolizumab activated innate immune metabolism and functions in primary OTC, which were accompanied by tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data and immunofluorescence analysis presented in the results.

claim: Pembrolizumab-induced activation of innate immune metabolism and functions in primary OTC was accompanied by tissue damage.
source: Pembrolizumab activated innate immune metabolism and functions in primary OTC, which were accompanied by tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by H&E staining and mIF analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: DSP analysis indicated an overall decrease in immunosuppressive macrophages and T cells in Pembrolizumab-treated primary OTC.
source: DSP analysis indicated an overall decrease in immunosuppressive macrophages and T cells but revealed microheterogeneity in immune responses and tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data presented in Figure 4D.

claim: DSP analysis revealed microheterogeneity in immune responses and tissue damage in Pembrolizumab-treated primary OTC.
source: DSP analysis indicated an overall decrease in immunosuppressive macrophages and T cells but revealed microheterogeneity in immune responses and tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by ROI-specific analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Two TMEs with altered cancer cell properties showed resistance to Pembrolizumab.
source: Two TMEs with altered cancer cell properties showed resistance.
evidence: This is inferred from DSP analysis of ROIs 6 and 8 showing different responses.

claim: Pembrolizumab or WGP alone had negligible effects on BM-lung cancer OTC.
source: Pembrolizumab or WGP alone had negligible effects on BM-lung cancer OTC but Pembrolizumab + WGP blocked central metabolism with increased pro-inflammatory effector release and tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic data in Figure 5 showing minimal changes with single treatments.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP blocked central metabolism in BM-lung cancer OTC.
source: Pembrolizumab or WGP alone had negligible effects on BM-lung cancer OTC but Pembrolizumab + WGP blocked central metabolism with increased pro-inflammatory effector release and tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP increased pro-inflammatory effector release in BM-lung cancer OTC.
source: Pembrolizumab or WGP alone had negligible effects on BM-lung cancer OTC but Pembrolizumab + WGP blocked central metabolism with increased pro-inflammatory effector release and tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine analysis data in Figure 6A-D.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP caused tissue damage in BM-lung cancer OTC.
source: Pembrolizumab or WGP alone had negligible effects on BM-lung cancer OTC but Pembrolizumab + WGP blocked central metabolism with increased pro-inflammatory effector release and tissue damage.
evidence: This is supported by mIF staining data in Figure 6E-H.

claim: Checkpoint inhibitor-based immunotherapy using PD-1 antibody Pembrolizumab has significantly improved the survival of lung and other cancer patients.
source: New checkpoint inhibitor-based immunotherapy, such as the use of programmed death one receptor (PD-1, CD279, or PDCD1) antibody Pembrolizumab (Pembro) has significantly improved the survival of lung and other cancer patients.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations in the introduction.

claim: Even after stratification, a large fraction of the patient population shows variable efficacy, resistance development, and intolerable toxicity to Pembrolizumab.
source: However, even after stratification, a large fraction of the patient population shows variable efficacy, resistance development, and intolerable toxicity (Arlauckas et al., 2017; Ayers et al., 2017; Garon et al., 2015; Meyers et al., 2018; Morgensztern and Herbst, 2016; Rizvi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Functional heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment is crucial to modulating drug responses including resistance development.
source: Functional heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial to modulating drug responses including resistance development (Dalton, 1999; Ostman, 2012; Qu et al., 2019; Trédan et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: O. Warburg pioneered the use of tissue slices and demonstrated enhanced lactic fermentation under aerobic conditions.
source: The use of tissue slices (with no culturing involved) was pioneered by O. Warburg who demonstrated enhanced lactic fermentation under aerobic conditions (Warburg, 1924), which is now recognized as a hallmark of cancers (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Warburg, 1924.

claim: Enhanced lactic fermentation under aerobic conditions is now recognized as a hallmark of cancers.
source: The use of tissue slices (with no culturing involved) was pioneered by O. Warburg who demonstrated enhanced lactic fermentation under aerobic conditions (Warburg, 1924), which is now recognized as a hallmark of cancers (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011.

claim: Ex vivo lung tissue slice cultures recapitulate the metabolic reprogramming observed in vivo.
source: We have shown that such ex vivo cultures recapitulate the metabolic reprogramming observed in vivo (Sellers et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The organotypic tissue culture model retains patients' native 3D architecture/tissue microenvironment including infiltrated immune cells.
source: This model is versatile in experimental manipulations and retains patients' native 3D architecture/tissue microenvironment including infiltrated immune cells, which is not represented by multiply passaged mouse PDX or 3D cell models including PDO.
evidence: This is a description of the model characteristics based on the authors' experience.

claim: The matched cancer and non-cancer tissue design provides the capacity for distinguishing on- and off-target drug actions in individual patients.
source: Furthermore, the matched cancer (CA) and non-cancer (NC) tissue design provides the capacity for distinguishing on- and off-target drug actions in individual patients (Lane et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Two different PD lung OTC treated with β-glucan displayed distinct responses of macrophage metabolism that was related to variable tissue damage.
source: We previously showed that two different PD lung OTC treated with the natural product immune activator (β-glucan) displayed distinct responses of macrophage (MΦ) metabolism that was related to variable tissue damage (Fan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Metabolic reprogramming is crucial to immune cell activation to meet the demand for energy/anabolic metabolism.
source: It is now widely recognized that metabolic reprogramming is crucial to immune cell activation to meet the demand for energy/anabolic metabolism (Gnanaprakasam et al., 2017; O'Neill and Pearce, 2016; Palmieri et al., 2020) and specific immunomodulatory events.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Succinate production in macrophages stabilized HIF1α, resulting in the release of proinflammatory IL-1β.
source: Notably, succinate production in MΦ stabilized HIF1α, resulting in the release of proinflammatory IL-1β (Tannahill et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tannahill et al., 2013.

claim: Tryptophan catabolism to quinolinate fuels de novo NAD+ synthesis.
source: Tryptophan (Trp) catabolism to quinolinate fuels de novo NAD+ synthesis and blockade of this pathway led to a pro-inflammatory state in aged MΦ (Minhas et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Minhas et al., 2019.

claim: Blockade of tryptophan catabolism to quinolinate led to a pro-inflammatory state in aged macrophages.
source: Tryptophan (Trp) catabolism to quinolinate fuels de novo NAD+ synthesis and blockade of this pathway led to a pro-inflammatory state in aged MΦ (Minhas et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Minhas et al., 2019.

claim: Enhanced glycolysis in cancer cells can deplete glucose leading to T-cell 'anergy' in the TME.
source: For example, enhanced glycolysis (e.g. induced by the expression of checkpoint ligand PD-L1) in cancer cells can deplete glucose leading to T-cell 'anergy' in the TME (Chang et al., 2015; Fischer et al., 2007; Lim et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Excess release of lactate and protons into the TME can deactivate infiltrating macrophages and T cells.
source: The resulting excess release of lactate and protons into the TME can also deactivate infiltrating MΦ and T cells (Fischer et al., 2007; Gurusamy et al., 2017; Munn and Bronte, 2016; Parker et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Expression of PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell function and survival by modulating T-cell metabolism.
source: The expression of PD-L1 receptor, PD-1 was also shown to negatively regulate T-cell function and survival by modulating T-cell metabolism (Bettonville et al., 2018; Patsoukis et al., 2015; Tkachev et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Tumor indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase depleted tryptophan in the TME by oxidation to kynurenine, which led to T-cell inhibition.
source: Moreover, tumor indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) depleted Trp in the TME by oxidation to kynurenine, which led to T-cell inhibition (Joyce and Fearon, 2015; Munn and Mellor, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Joyce and Fearon, 2015; Munn and Mellor, 2013.

claim: The UK131 tumor stained positive for KRT5.
source: As shown in Supplementary file 2, the UK131 tumor stained positive for KRT5 (A), which is consistent with its clinical classification as lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) (Xiao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: KRT5 positivity is consistent with clinical classification as lung squamous cell carcinoma.
source: As shown in Supplementary file 2, the UK131 tumor stained positive for KRT5 (A), which is consistent with its clinical classification as lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) (Xiao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xiao et al., 2017.

claim: KRT5+ cancer cells in UK131 tumor were positive for HIF1α, with staining occurring more in the cytoplasm than in the nucleus.
source: Although the KRT5+ cancer cells were positive for HIF1α, this staining occurred much more in the cytoplasm than in the nucleus, which suggests that the major fraction of HIF1α was not transcriptionally active.
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence staining patterns observed in Supplementary file 2.

claim: The major fraction of HIF1α in UK131 tumor cancer cells was not transcriptionally active.
source: Although the KRT5+ cancer cells were positive for HIF1α, this staining occurred much more in the cytoplasm than in the nucleus, which suggests that the major fraction of HIF1α was not transcriptionally active.
evidence: This is inferred from the cytoplasmic localization of HIF1α staining.

claim: Smaller non-cancer HIF1α+ cells present in UK131 tumor are likely infiltrated immune cells.
source: Also present were the smaller non-cancer HIF1α+ cells, which are likely infiltrated immune cells (A).
evidence: This is inferred from cell size and morphology in immunofluorescence images.

claim: PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells are present in UK131 tumor.
source: More notable was the presence of PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells (B), which indicates a high likelihood of this tissue to respond to Pembro treatment.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: The presence of PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells indicates a high likelihood of UK131 tissue to respond to Pembrolizumab treatment.
source: More notable was the presence of PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells (B), which indicates a high likelihood of this tissue to respond to Pembro treatment.
evidence: This is inferred based on the mechanism of action of Pembrolizumab.

claim: PD-L1 expressing CD206+ cells are present in UK131 tumor.
source: Also evident were PD-L1 expressing CD206+ cells (C), which are characteristic of tumor-associated MΦ (TAM) (Van Overmeire et al., 2014) and reflective of an immunosuppressive TME (Lu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: PD-L1 expressing CD206+ cells are characteristic of tumor-associated macrophages.
source: Also evident were PD-L1 expressing CD206+ cells (C), which are characteristic of tumor-associated MΦ (TAM) (Van Overmeire et al., 2014) and reflective of an immunosuppressive TME (Lu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Van Overmeire et al., 2014.

claim: PD-L1 expressing CD206+ cells are reflective of an immunosuppressive TME.
source: Also evident were PD-L1 expressing CD206+ cells (C), which are characteristic of tumor-associated MΦ (TAM) (Van Overmeire et al., 2014) and reflective of an immunosuppressive TME (Lu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2019.

claim: Positive mIF staining of chromogranin A and NCAM1 confirmed the clinical classification of UK2035 tumor as a lung neuroendocrine tumor.
source: Positive mIF staining of chromogranin A (CgA) and NCAM1 (Supplementary file 3) confirmed the clinical classification of the metastatic UK2035 tumor as a lung neuroendocrine tumor (Kashiwagi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data in Supplementary file 3 and citation.

claim: PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells and PD-L1+ cells are present in UK2035 tumor.
source: PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells and PD-L1+ cells were also present in this tumor, with the former cells far fewer in numbers than the latter cells (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data in Supplementary file 3.

claim: PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells are far fewer in numbers than PD-L1+ cells in UK2035 tumor.
source: PD-1 expressing CD8+ T cells and PD-L1+ cells were also present in this tumor, with the former cells far fewer in numbers than the latter cells (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is based on quantitative assessment of immunofluorescence staining.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C6-Glc-derived 13C labeling in most of the PPP metabolites in UK131 CA OTC compared to control.
source: Namely, Pembro enhanced 13C6-Glc-derived 13C labeling in most of the PPP metabolites compared to the control (Ctl) (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C labeling of 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate in UK131 CA OTC.
source: These included 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) (6, a), 13C5-ribulose/ribose-5-phosphate (R5P) (5, c), 13C7-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate (S7P) (7, d), 13C4-erythrose-4-phosphate (E4P) (4, e), and 13C6-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) (6, f), but not 13C6-6-phosphogluconate (6 PG) (6, b).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 1a.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C labeling of 13C5-ribulose/ribose-5-phosphate in UK131 CA OTC.
source: These included 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) (6, a), 13C5-ribulose/ribose-5-phosphate (R5P) (5, c), 13C7-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate (S7P) (7, d), 13C4-erythrose-4-phosphate (E4P) (4, e), and 13C6-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) (6, f), but not 13C6-6-phosphogluconate (6 PG) (6, b).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 1c.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C labeling of 13C7-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate in UK131 CA OTC.
source: These included 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) (6, a), 13C5-ribulose/ribose-5-phosphate (R5P) (5, c), 13C7-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate (S7P) (7, d), 13C4-erythrose-4-phosphate (E4P) (4, e), and 13C6-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) (6, f), but not 13C6-6-phosphogluconate (6 PG) (6, b).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 1d.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C labeling of 13C4-erythrose-4-phosphate in UK131 CA OTC.
source: These included 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) (6, a), 13C5-ribulose/ribose-5-phosphate (R5P) (5, c), 13C7-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate (S7P) (7, d), 13C4-erythrose-4-phosphate (E4P) (4, e), and 13C6-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) (6, f), but not 13C6-6-phosphogluconate (6 PG) (6, b).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 1e.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C labeling of 13C6-fructose-6-phosphate in UK131 CA OTC.
source: These included 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) (6, a), 13C5-ribulose/ribose-5-phosphate (R5P) (5, c), 13C7-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate (S7P) (7, d), 13C4-erythrose-4-phosphate (E4P) (4, e), and 13C6-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) (6, f), but not 13C6-6-phosphogluconate (6 PG) (6, b).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 1f.

claim: Pembrolizumab did not enhance 13C labeling of 13C6-6-phosphogluconate in UK131 CA OTC.
source: These included 13C6-glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) (6, a), 13C5-ribulose/ribose-5-phosphate (R5P) (5, c), 13C7-sedoheptulose-7-phosphate (S7P) (7, d), 13C4-erythrose-4-phosphate (E4P) (4, e), and 13C6-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) (6, f), but not 13C6-6-phosphogluconate (6 PG) (6, b).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 1b.

claim: The non-oxidative branch reactions catalyzed by transketolase and transaldolase contributed more to 13C incorporation into R5P, S7P, E4P, and F6P in Pembrolizumab versus control-treated CA OTC.
source: As such, the non-oxidative (Nonox) branch reactions catalyzed by the transketolase (TK) and transaldolase (TA) contributed more to the 13C incorporation into R5P, S7P, E4P, and F6P in Pembro versus Ctl-treated CA OTC.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of 13C labeling in PPP metabolites.

claim: Pembrolizumab induced higher buildup of scrambled 13C isotopologues of PPP metabolites in UK131 CA OTC.
source: This agrees with the Pembro-induced higher buildup of scrambled 13C isotopologues (Scr) of these metabolites (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1 showing scrambled isotopologue patterns.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C labeling of glycogen in UK131 CA OTC.
source: In addition to PPP activation, Pembro enhanced 13C labeling of glycogen (i) and its direct precursor UDP-glucose (UDPG, h) (Figure 1), which suggests stimulation of glycogen synthesis by Pembro.
evidence: This is supported by NMR data in Figure 1i.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced 13C labeling of UDP-glucose in UK131 CA OTC.
source: In addition to PPP activation, Pembro enhanced 13C labeling of glycogen (i) and its direct precursor UDP-glucose (UDPG, h) (Figure 1), which suggests stimulation of glycogen synthesis by Pembro.
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 1h.

claim: Pembrolizumab stimulated glycogen synthesis in UK131 CA OTC.
source: In addition to PPP activation, Pembro enhanced 13C labeling of glycogen (i) and its direct precursor UDP-glucose (UDPG, h) (Figure 1), which suggests stimulation of glycogen synthesis by Pembro.
evidence: This is inferred from enhanced 13C labeling of glycogen and its precursor.

claim: None of the Pembrolizumab-induced metabolic changes in PPP and glycogen synthesis were evident in matched NC OTC.
source: None of these changes were evident in the matched NC OTC, which indicates that these effects are tumor specific.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of CA and NC data in Figure 1.

claim: Pembrolizumab effects on PPP and glycogen synthesis are tumor specific.
source: None of these changes were evident in the matched NC OTC, which indicates that these effects are tumor specific.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of changes in NC tissue.

claim: Pembrolizumab moderately increased 13C-Gln uptake in UK131 CA OTC compared with control.
source: With 13C5,15N2-Gln as tracer, Pembro moderately increased 13C-Gln uptake in CA OTC, compared with the Ctl.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic data in Figure 2A-a.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced release of 13C-Glu into the medium in UK131 CA OTC.
source: This was accompanied by enhanced release of 13C-Glu and 13C-succinate into the medium (Figure 2A–a), which could at least in part account for Pembro-induced increase in Gln uptake.
evidence: This is supported by NMR data in Figure 2A-a.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced release of 13C-succinate into the medium in UK131 CA OTC.
source: This was accompanied by enhanced release of 13C-Glu and 13C-succinate into the medium (Figure 2A–a), which could at least in part account for Pembro-induced increase in Gln uptake.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2A-a.

claim: Enhanced release of 13C-Glu and 13C-succinate could at least in part account for Pembrolizumab-induced increase in Gln uptake.
source: This was accompanied by enhanced release of 13C-Glu and 13C-succinate into the medium (Figure 2A–a), which could at least in part account for Pembro-induced increase in Gln uptake.
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic data.

claim: Pembrolizumab had only minor changes in glucose uptake and lactate release into the medium in UK131 CA OTC.
source: In comparison, there were only minor changes in the glucose uptake and lactate released into the medium (Figure 2A–b).
evidence: This is supported by NMR data in Figure 2A-b.

claim: Pembrolizumab enhanced glutaminolysis but had a negligible effect on glycolysis in UK131 CA OTC.
source: Thus, Pembro enhanced glutaminolysis (Gln conversion to Glu and succinate) but had a negligible effect on glycolysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic tracing data.

claim: Pembrolizumab modestly depleted 13C5-Glu and 13C5-αKG in UK131 CA OTC.
source: In CA OTC, Pembro modestly depleted the first two products 13C5-Glu (C5Nx, a)/ 13C5-αKG (C5, b) and subsequent Krebs cycle products (13C4- and other 13C-isotopologues of succinate, fumarate, malate, citrate, and Asp) (c–g).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 2B-a,b.

claim: Pembrolizumab depleted subsequent Krebs cycle products including 13C4- and other 13C-isotopologues of succinate, fumarate, malate, citrate, and Asp in UK131 CA OTC.
source: In CA OTC, Pembro modestly depleted the first two products 13C5-Glu (C5Nx, a)/ 13C5-αKG (C5, b) and subsequent Krebs cycle products (13C4- and other 13C-isotopologues of succinate, fumarate, malate, citrate, and Asp) (c–g).
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 2B-c to g.

claim: 13C labeling of glutathione was less affected by Pembrolizumab treatment in UK131 CA OTC.
source: 13C labeling of glutathione (GSH, h) was less affected by the Pembro treatment.
evidence: This is supported by IC-UHR-FTMS data in Figure 2B-h.

claim: Blockade of glutaminase activity and/or diversion of Glu to GSH metabolism could account for Pembrolizumab-induced changes in 13C labeling patterns of tissue metabolites.
source: Blockade of the glutaminase (GLS) activity and/or diversion of Glu to GSH metabolism could account for these Pembro-induced changes in the 13C labeling patterns of tissue metabolites.
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic data patterns.

claim: GSH synthesis requires cystine uptake from the medium in exchange for Glu release via the xCT antiporter.
source: In addition, GSH synthesis requires cystine uptake from the medium in exchange for Glu release via the xCT antiporter (Shih et al., 2006), which would contribute to the buildup of 13C-Glu in the medium and add to the depletion of tissue 13C-Glu.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shih et al., 2006.

claim: xCT antiporter-mediated Glu release would contribute to the buildup of 13C-Glu in the medium and add to the depletion of tissue 13C-Glu.
source: In addition, GSH synthesis requires cystine uptake from the medium in exchange for Glu release via the xCT antiporter (Shih et al., 2006), which would contribute to the buildup of 13C-Glu in the medium and add to the depletion of tissue 13C-Glu.
evidence: This is inferred from the mechanism of xCT antiporter.

claim: Increased release of 13C-succinate to the medium would further deplete tissue succinate.
source: Likewise, increased release of 13C-succinate to the medium would further deplete tissue succinate.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the metabolic data.

claim: None of the Pembrolizumab-induced changes in glutamine metabolism were evident in matched NC counterparts.
source: Again, none of these changes were evident in the matched NC counterparts.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of CA and NC data in Figure 2.

claim: Activation of the PPP and glycogen metabolism occurs during proinflammatory or M1-type polarization of murine macrophages and model human macrophages THP-1 cells by lipopolysaccharides.
source: Activation of the PPP and glycogen metabolism is known to occur during proinflammatory or M1-type polarization of murine MΦ and model human MΦ THP-1 cells by lipopolysaccharides (LPS) (Ma et al., 2020; Nagy and Haschemi, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ma et al., 2020; Nagy and Haschemi, 2015.

claim: PPP and glycogen metabolism via PPP help sustain NADPH production in activated macrophages to maintain redox homeostasis and fuel the demand for lipid and deoxynucleotide synthesis.
source: PPP and glycogen metabolism via PPP (Ma et al., 2020) help sustain NADPH production in activated MΦ to maintain redox homeostasis and fuel the demand for lipid and deoxynucleotide synthesis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ma et al., 2020.

claim: M1- versus M2-type human macrophages showed very similar shift in 13C labeling patterns of PPP and glycogen products as those observed for Pembrolizumab- versus control-treated CA OTC.
source: Comparing M1- versus M2-type MΦ, we saw very similar shift in the 13C labeling patterns of the PPP and glycogen products (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) as those observed for the Pembro- versus Ctl-treated CA OTC (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of data in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a break in G6P to 6PG conversion in M1- versus M2-type human macrophages.
source: Particularly noted were the break in G6P (a) to 6 PG (b) conversion and the enhanced buildup of 13C scrambled products of PPP (c–f) in M1- versus M2-type MΦ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1); the latter is consistent with Nonox PPP being the major source of pentose phosphates in LPS-activated murine MΦ (Haschemi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Enhanced buildup of 13C scrambled products of PPP occurred in M1- versus M2-type human macrophages.
source: Particularly noted were the break in G6P (a) to 6 PG (b) conversion and the enhanced buildup of 13C scrambled products of PPP (c–f) in M1- versus M2-type MΦ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1); the latter is consistent with Nonox PPP being the major source of pentose phosphates in LPS-activated murine MΦ (Haschemi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Non-oxidative PPP is the major source of pentose phosphates in LPS-activated murine macrophages.
source: Particularly noted were the break in G6P (a) to 6 PG (b) conversion and the enhanced buildup of 13C scrambled products of PPP (c–f) in M1- versus M2-type MΦ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1); the latter is consistent with Nonox PPP being the major source of pentose phosphates in LPS-activated murine MΦ (Haschemi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Haschemi et al., 2012.

claim: M1 polarization of human macrophages induced similar shifts in 13C5,15N2-Gln metabolism as those elicited by Pembrolizumab in CA OTC.
source: We also observed similarities in the shift of 13C5,15N2-Gln metabolism induced by M1 polarization of human MΦ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) compared with those elicited by Pembro in CA OTC (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of data in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: M1 polarization of human macrophages enhanced release of 13C-succinate.
source: These included enhanced release of 13C-succinate (A–a), lack of effect on the excretion of glycolytic lactate, reduced Gln oxidation through glutaminolysis and the Krebs cycle (B–a to g), and lack of attenuation in GSH synthesis (B–h) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-a.

claim: M1 polarization of human macrophages had no effect on the excretion of glycolytic lactate.
source: These included enhanced release of 13C-succinate (A–a), lack of effect on the excretion of glycolytic lactate, reduced Gln oxidation through glutaminolysis and the Krebs cycle (B–a to g), and lack of attenuation in GSH synthesis (B–h) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: M1 polarization of human macrophages reduced Gln oxidation through glutaminolysis and the Krebs cycle.
source: These included enhanced release of 13C-succinate (A–a), lack of effect on the excretion of glycolytic lactate, reduced Gln oxidation through glutaminolysis and the Krebs cycle (B–a to g), and lack of attenuation in GSH synthesis (B–h) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-a to g.

claim: M1 polarization of human macrophages showed no attenuation in GSH synthesis.
source: These included enhanced release of 13C-succinate (A–a), lack of effect on the excretion of glycolytic lactate, reduced Gln oxidation through glutaminolysis and the Krebs cycle (B–a to g), and lack of attenuation in GSH synthesis (B–h) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-h.

claim: M1 versus M2-type human macrophages showed reduced 13C-Glu release.
source: However, some differential responses were also evident, notably reduced 13C-Glu release (A–a) as well as increased buildup of 13C-itaconate (A–c) and unlabeled quinolinate (QA, A–d) in M1 versus M2-type Mϕ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) as opposed to the lack of or opposite effect observed for Pembro- versus Ctl-treated CA OTC (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-a.

claim: M1 versus M2-type human macrophages showed increased buildup of 13C-itaconate.
source: However, some differential responses were also evident, notably reduced 13C-Glu release (A–a) as well as increased buildup of 13C-itaconate (A–c) and unlabeled quinolinate (QA, A–d) in M1 versus M2-type Mϕ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) as opposed to the lack of or opposite effect observed for Pembro- versus Ctl-treated CA OTC (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-c.

claim: M1 versus M2-type human macrophages showed increased buildup of unlabeled quinolinate.
source: However, some differential responses were also evident, notably reduced 13C-Glu release (A–a) as well as increased buildup of 13C-itaconate (A–c) and unlabeled quinolinate (QA, A–d) in M1 versus M2-type Mϕ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) as opposed to the lack of or opposite effect observed for Pembro- versus Ctl-treated CA OTC (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-d.

claim: Differences between M1 macrophage responses and Pembrolizumab-treated CA OTC responses could reflect the influence of TME on macrophage metabolism and/or metabolic contribution of other cell types in the TME.
source: These differences could reflect the influence of TME on MΦ metabolism and/or metabolic contribution of other cell types in the TME.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed differences between isolated macrophages and tissue cultures.

claim: The release of proinflammatory cytokines/chemokines into the media was consistently enhanced by Pembrolizumab treatment of UK131 CA OTC.
source: Besides metabolic shifts, we examined the culture media for secreted immune effectors. The release of proinflammatory cytokines/chemokines into the media was consistently enhanced by the Pembro treatment of CA OTC, as shown in Figure 3A–F.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine analysis data in Figure 3A-F.

claim: Some Pembrolizumab-induced changes in cytokine release were evident in NSCLC tumor PDOs.
source: Some of these Pembro-induced changes were evident in NSCLC tumor PDOs (Mediavilla-Varela et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mediavilla-Varela et al., 2017.

claim: None of the Pembrolizumab effects on cytokine release in UK131 CA OTC reached statistical significance of p-value ≤ 0.05.
source: Although the none of the Pembro effects on CA OTC reached statistical significance of p-value ≤ 0.05, consistent trend was seen that points to M1 type polarization.
evidence: This is stated based on statistical analysis of the data.

claim: Consistent trend in cytokine release points to M1 type polarization in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA OTC.
source: Although the none of the Pembro effects on CA OTC reached statistical significance of p-value ≤ 0.05, consistent trend was seen that points to M1 type polarization.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of cytokine changes.

claim: M1- versus M2-polarized human macrophages showed increased release of IL-6, TNFα, IL-8, MIP-1α, IFNγ, and IFNα2.
source: This is corroborated by the increased release of the same set of effectors (IL-6, TNFα [Mercalli et al., 2013], IL-8 [Meniailo et al., 2018], MIP-1α or CCL3 [Maurer and von Stebut, 2004], IFNγ, and IFNα2 [Kumagai et al., 2007]) in M1- versus M2-polarized human MΦ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and multiple citations.

claim: MIP-1 are chemokines that regulate both pro-inflammatory responses and homeostasis (wound healing).
source: It is interesting to note that MIP-1 are chemokines that regulate both pro-inflammatory responses and homeostasis (wound healing; Maurer and von Stebut, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Maurer and von Stebut, 2004.

claim: Histological analysis of Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA OTC sections by H&E staining revealed extensive tissue damages including the presence of macrophages in apoptotic regions.
source: Histological analysis of Pembro-treated CA OTC sections by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining revealed extensive tissue damages including the presence of MΦ in apoptotic regions, as shown in Figure 4A.
evidence: This is supported by H&E staining images in Figure 4A.

claim: mIF staining of Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA OTC confirmed increased apoptosis.
source: mIF staining of separate sections of the same OTC confirmed increased apoptosis (red caspase fluorescence), which was accompanied by decreased mitotic index (green PCNA fluorescence) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by mIF staining data in Figure 4B.

claim: Pembrolizumab treatment of UK131 CA OTC was accompanied by decreased mitotic index.
source: mIF staining of separate sections of the same OTC confirmed increased apoptosis (red caspase fluorescence), which was accompanied by decreased mitotic index (green PCNA fluorescence) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by mIF staining data in Figure 4B.

claim: Pembrolizumab treatment of UK131 CA OTC resulted in decrease in KRT5+/PD-L1+, KRT5+ cancer cell populations.
source: Also evident were the decrease in KRT5+/PD-L1+, KRT5+ cancer cell as well as PD-1+ and PD-1+/CD8+ T-cell populations.
evidence: This is supported by mIF staining data in Figure 4B.

claim: Pembrolizumab treatment of UK131 CA OTC resulted in decrease in PD-1+ and PD-1+/CD8+ T-cell populations.
source: Also evident were the decrease in KRT5+/PD-L1+, KRT5+ cancer cell as well as PD-1+ and PD-1+/CD8+ T-cell populations.
evidence: This is supported by mIF staining data in Figure 4B.

claim: UK131 CA OTC response to Pembrolizumab is expected based on Pembrolizumab-mediated activation of exhausted PD-1+ T cells that possess anti-tumor activity.
source: The CA OTC response is expected based on Pembro-mediated activation of exhausted PD-1+ T cells that possess anti-tumor activity (Graves et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graves et al., 2019.

claim: DSP analysis of UK131 CA OTC revealed 11 markers whose expression was attenuated across most ROIs of Pembrolizumab-treated versus control tissue sections.
source: ROI-dependent analysis of 58 protein markers revealed 11 markers whose expression was attenuated across most ROIs of Pembro-treated versus Ctl tissue sections (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4D.

claim: Ki67 expression was attenuated across most ROIs of Pembrolizumab-treated versus control UK131 CA tissue sections.
source: These included Ki67 as well as cancer cell markers EpCAM and Her2.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4D.

claim: Cancer cell markers EpCAM and Her2 expression were attenuated across most ROIs of Pembrolizumab-treated versus control UK131 CA tissue sections.
source: These included Ki67 as well as cancer cell markers EpCAM and Her2.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4D.

claim: Decreased expression of Ki67, EpCAM, and Her2 is consistent with tissue damage and reduced cancer cell population observed by H&E and mIF imaging.
source: The decreased expression is consistent with tissue damage and reduced cancer cell population as observed by H&E and mIF imaging (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is inferred from correlation of DSP data with imaging data.

claim: Pembrolizumab treatment reduced expression of M2-type macrophage markers CD163 and Arg1 in UK131 CA OTC.
source: Also evident was the reduced expression of M2-type MΦ markers, CD163 and Arg1 as well as regulatory T (Treg) cell marker CD25.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4D.

claim: Pembrolizumab treatment reduced expression of regulatory T cell marker CD25 in UK131 CA OTC.
source: Also evident was the reduced expression of M2-type MΦ markers, CD163 and Arg1 as well as regulatory T (Treg) cell marker CD25.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4D.

claim: CD25+ Treg cells induce M2-type polarization in co-cultured monocytes, as evidenced by upregulation of CD163 and downregulation of HLA-DR expression.
source: CD25+ Treg cells are known to induce M2-type polarization in co-cultured monocytes, as evidenced by the upregulation of CD163 and downregulation of HLA-DR expression (Tiemessen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tiemessen et al., 2007.

claim: CD25 suppression may be related to reduced CD163 expression in Pembrolizumab-treated TME.
source: Thus, CD25 suppression may be related to reduced CD163 expression in the Pembro-treated TME.
evidence: This is inferred from the relationship between Treg cells and M2 polarization.

claim: There was an overall increase in the ratio of M1-macrophage marker HLA-DR to M2-macrophage marker Arg1 in Pembrolizumab- versus control-treated UK131 CA tissues.
source: Although there was no consistent increase in HLA-DR expression across ROIs, we saw an overall increase in the ratio of this M1–MΦ marker to the M2–MΦ marker Arg1 in Pembro- versus Ctl-treated CA tissues (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: There was an overall increase in the ratio of M1-macrophage marker IDO1 to M2-macrophage marker Arg1 in Pembrolizumab- versus control-treated UK131 CA tissues.
source: This was also the case for another human M1–MΦ marker IDO1.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: DSP data point to repolarization of M2- to M1-type macrophages in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissue.
source: These data point to repolarization of M2- to M1-type MΦ in the Pembro-treated CA tissue.
evidence: This is inferred from the changes in M1 and M2 marker ratios.

claim: The ratio of T-cell activation marker iCOS to T-cell marker CD4 largely increased in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissue.
source: In contrast to the response of the Treg marker CD25, the ratio of a T-cell activation marker iCOS (Dong et al., 2001) to T-cell marker CD4 largely increased (Figure 4E) along with decreased expression of the checkpoint protein CTLA4 (Figure 4D) across all ROIs in response to Pembro.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: Expression of checkpoint protein CTLA4 decreased across all ROIs in response to Pembrolizumab in UK131 CA tissue.
source: In contrast to the response of the Treg marker CD25, the ratio of a T-cell activation marker iCOS (Dong et al., 2001) to T-cell marker CD4 largely increased (Figure 4E) along with decreased expression of the checkpoint protein CTLA4 (Figure 4D) across all ROIs in response to Pembro.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4D.

claim: Reduced Treg cell occurrence was commonly noted in CA tissues from Pembrolizumab-treated cancer patients.
source: Reduced Treg cell occurrence was commonly noted in CA tissues from Pembro-treated cancer patients (Kumar et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kumar et al., 2020.

claim: Enhanced iCOS expression in T cells was not known to be induced by anti-PD-1 treatment.
source: However, enhanced iCOS expression in T cells was not known to be induced by anti-PD-1 treatment (Wei et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wei et al., 2017.

claim: No immune cell infiltration can occur in the OTC model.
source: It should be noted that since no immune cell infiltration can occur in our OTC model, the Pembro-induced T-cell or MΦ marker response was derived from the resident populations only.
evidence: This is a characteristic of the ex vivo OTC model.

claim: Pembrolizumab-induced T-cell or macrophage marker response in OTC was derived from resident populations only.
source: It should be noted that since no immune cell infiltration can occur in our OTC model, the Pembro-induced T-cell or MΦ marker response was derived from the resident populations only.
evidence: This is inferred from the nature of the OTC model.

claim: PanCK+ cancer cells-rich ROIs 3, 7, 9, and 12 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissues had much higher granzyme B relative to Ki-67 levels than ROIs 6 and 8.
source: In particular for Pembro-treated tissues, panCK+ cancer cells-rich ROIs 3, 7, 9, and 12 had much higher granzyme B (GZMB) relative to Ki-67 levels than ROIs 6 and 8.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: ROIs 3, 7, 9, and 12 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissues displayed higher iCOS/CD4 ratios than ROIs 6 and 8.
source: ROIs 3, 7, 9, and 12 also displayed higher iCOS/CD4 ratios than ROIs 6 and 8.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: ROIs 3, 7, 9, and 12 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissues have more activated T cells and reduced proliferative capacity of cancer cells than ROIs 6 and 8.
source: These data point to more activated T cells and reduced proliferative capacity of cancer cells in the former than the latter regions.
evidence: This is inferred from the GZMB/Ki-67 and iCOS/CD4 ratios.

claim: Attenuated expression of lung cancer driver protein Her2 was noted in ROIs 6/8 versus ROIs 3/7/9/12 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissues.
source: We also noted attenuated expression of a lung cancer driver protein Her2 (Garrido-Castro and Felip, 2013) in ROIs 6/8 versus ROIs 3/7/9/12, which suggests a difference in cancer cell property between the two sets of ROIs.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: Her2 is a lung cancer driver protein.
source: We also noted attenuated expression of a lung cancer driver protein Her2 (Garrido-Castro and Felip, 2013) in ROIs 6/8 versus ROIs 3/7/9/12, which suggests a difference in cancer cell property between the two sets of ROIs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Garrido-Castro and Felip, 2013.

claim: Differential Her2 expression suggests a difference in cancer cell property between ROIs 6/8 and ROIs 3/7/9/12 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissues.
source: We also noted attenuated expression of a lung cancer driver protein Her2 (Garrido-Castro and Felip, 2013) in ROIs 6/8 versus ROIs 3/7/9/12, which suggests a difference in cancer cell property between the two sets of ROIs.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential Her2 expression patterns.

claim: ROI 6 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissue displayed very high IDO1/Arg1 and HLA-DR/Arg1 ratios compared to other ROIs including ROI 8.
source: Moreover, ROI six displayed very high IDO1/Arg1 and HLA-DR/Arg1 ratios than other ROIs including ROI 8.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: High IDO1/Arg1 and HLA-DR/Arg1 ratios in ROI 6 could reflect particularly high polarization of TAM toward M1-type and/or IDO1 overexpression in cancer cells.
source: This could reflect a particularly high polarization of TAM toward M1-type and/or IDO1 overexpression in cancer cells in ROI 6.
evidence: This is inferred from the marker ratio patterns.

claim: Cancer cells in ROI 6 TME appeared to remain proliferative despite high M1 polarization.
source: In either case, cancer cells in this TME appeared to remain proliferative.
evidence: This is inferred from the Ki-67 levels in context of other markers.

claim: ROI 8 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissue had the highest proliferative capacity with the lowest IDO1 or HLA-DR to Arg1 ratios.
source: As for ROI 8, the proliferative capacity was the highest with the lowest IDO1 or HLA-DR to Arg1 ratios but a comparable level of cytotoxic GZMB and ICOS/CD4 ratio to those of ROIs 3/7/9/12.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: ROI 8 in Pembrolizumab-treated UK131 CA tissue had a comparable level of cytotoxic GZMB and ICOS/CD4 ratio to those of ROIs 3/7/9/12.
source: As for ROI 8, the proliferative capacity was the highest with the lowest IDO1 or HLA-DR to Arg1 ratios but a comparable level of cytotoxic GZMB and ICOS/CD4 ratio to those of ROIs 3/7/9/12.
evidence: This is supported by DSP data in Figure 4E.

claim: Data implicate the presence of Pembrolizumab-resistant cancer cells in ROIs 6 and 8 of UK131 CA tissue.
source: These data implicate the presence of Pembro-resistant cancer cells in ROIs 6 and 8, which can overcome M1 polarization in ROI six and T-cell activation in ROI 8.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of proliferative capacity and immune marker patterns.

claim: Pembrolizumab-resistant cancer cells in ROI 6 can overcome M1 polarization.
source: These data implicate the presence of Pembro-resistant cancer cells in ROIs 6 and 8, which can overcome M1 polarization in ROI six and T-cell activation in ROI 8.
evidence: This is inferred from the maintained proliferation despite high M1 markers.

claim: Pembrolizumab-resistant cancer cells in ROI 8 can overcome T-cell activation.
source: These data implicate the presence of Pembro-resistant cancer cells in ROIs 6 and 8, which can overcome M1 polarization in ROI six and T-cell activation in ROI 8.
evidence: This is inferred from the maintained proliferation despite T-cell activation markers.

claim: If ROI 6 cancer cells were high in IDO1 activity, this can deplete Trp in the TME while producing immunosuppressive metabolites such as kynurenine.
source: If ROI six cancer cells were high in IDO1 activity, this can deplete Trp in the TME while producing immunosuppressive metabolites such as kynurenine, both of which could contribute to immune evasion (Li et al., 2019; Moffett and Namboodiri, 2003) and thus cancer cell resistance.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on known IDO1 function.

claim: Trp depletion and kynurenine production could contribute to immune evasion and cancer cell resistance.
source: If ROI six cancer cells were high in IDO1 activity, this can deplete Trp in the TME while producing immunosuppressive metabolites such as kynurenine, both of which could contribute to immune evasion (Li et al., 2019; Moffett and Namboodiri, 2003) and thus cancer cell resistance.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019; Moffett and Namboodiri, 2003.

claim: IDO1 overexpression occurred in NSCLC.
source: IDO1 overexpression occurred in NSCLC and higher serum kynurenine to Trp ratios/QA levels were associated with NSCLC disease progression (Bianco et al., 2019; Botticelli et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bianco et al., 2019; Botticelli et al., 2018.

claim: Higher serum kynurenine to Trp ratios/QA levels were associated with NSCLC disease progression.
source: IDO1 overexpression occurred in NSCLC and higher serum kynurenine to Trp ratios/QA levels were associated with NSCLC disease progression (Bianco et al., 2019; Botticelli et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bianco et al., 2019; Botticelli et al., 2018.

claim: QA built up in response to M1-macrophage activation.
source: Our metabolomic data showed that QA built up in response to M1-MΦ activation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which presumably resulted from a block in the downstream enzyme quinolinate phosphoribosyl-transferase, which is involved in de novo NAD+ synthesis (Minhas et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by metabolomic data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: QA buildup in M1-macrophages presumably resulted from a block in quinolinate phosphoribosyl-transferase, which is involved in de novo NAD+ synthesis.
source: Our metabolomic data showed that QA built up in response to M1-MΦ activation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which presumably resulted from a block in the downstream enzyme quinolinate phosphoribosyl-transferase, which is involved in de novo NAD+ synthesis (Minhas et al., 2019).
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic data and supported by citation.

claim: Trp-fueled NAD+ repletion is required for mitochondrial signaling and metabolism during immune resolution.
source: Trp-fueled NAD+ repletion is required for mitochondrial signaling and metabolism during immune resolution.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: QA depletion by Pembrolizumab in UK131 CA OTC is unlikely to result from M2-type macrophage polarization as Arg1 expression was down.
source: QA depletion by Pembro in CA OTC (Figure 2A–d) is unlikely to result from M2-type MΦ polarization as Arg1 expression was down (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of metabolic and protein expression data.

claim: QA depletion by Pembrolizumab in UK131 CA OTC is consistent with excess Trp consumption by IDO1-overexpressing cancer cells, thereby interfering with immune activation.
source: Instead, it is consistent with excess Trp consumption by IDO1-overexpressing cancer cells, thereby interfering with immune activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic data and IDO1 expression patterns.

claim: There were no consistent changes in 13C labeling of glycolytic and Krebs cycle intermediates or end products in UK2035 CA OTC in response to Pembrolizumab or WGP treatment.
source: We found no consistent changes in the 13C labeling of the glycolytic and Krebs cycle intermediates or end products in response to Pembro () or WGP () treatment (a, c–h), except for the WGP-elicited reduction of F1,6BP (b) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5A.

claim: WGP treatment elicited reduction of F1,6BP in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: We found no consistent changes in the 13C labeling of the glycolytic and Krebs cycle intermediates or end products in response to Pembro () or WGP () treatment (a, c–h), except for the WGP-elicited reduction of F1,6BP (b) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5A-b.

claim: There were no consistent changes in 13C labeling of GSH and itaconate derived from the Krebs cycle in UK2035 CA OTC in response to Pembrolizumab or WGP treatment.
source: Nor were there consistent changes for GSH and itaconate derived from the Krebs cycle (k–l).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5A.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP treatment blocked 13C incorporation into tissue F1,6BP, pyruvate, citrate, c-aconitate, Asp, and Glu in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: However, P + W treatment () blocked 13C incorporation into tissue F1,6BP, pyruvate (c), citrate (e), c-aconitate (f), Asp (i), and Glu (j) but not the uptake of 13C-Glc nor the release of 13C-Lac into media.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5A.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP treatment did not block the uptake of 13C-Glc nor the release of 13C-Lac into media in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: However, P + W treatment () blocked 13C incorporation into tissue F1,6BP, pyruvate (c), citrate (e), c-aconitate (f), Asp (i), and Glu (j) but not the uptake of 13C-Glc nor the release of 13C-Lac into media.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5A.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP disrupted the first half of the Krebs cycle activity (PDH to IDH), but not glycolysis as a whole in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: These data suggest that P + W disrupted the first half of the Krebs cycle activity (PDH to IDH), but not glycolysis as a whole.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of metabolic changes.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP treatment substantially depleted all major 13C labeled products of PPP in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: The combined P + W treatment substantially depleted all major 13C labeled products of PPP (a–f).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5B.

claim: Neither Pembrolizumab nor WGP treatment alone affected 13C labeling of PPP products except for depletion of 13C scrambled 6PG by WGP in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: Neither Pembro nor WGP treatment alone affected the 13C labeling of the PPP products except for the depletion of 13C scrambled 6 PG (Scr, b) by WGP.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5B.

claim: No depletion was evident for 6PG's precursor G6P and downstream products under WGP treatment in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: However, no depletion was evident for 6 PG's precursor, G6P (a) and downstream products (c–f) under WGP treatment.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5B.

claim: WGP-induced depletion of 6PG without affecting G6P and downstream products points to a block at G6PDH in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: These data point to a block at G6PDH, which agreed with WGP's capacity for M1 repolarization as such block was also evident in human M1–MΦ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic data pattern.

claim: WGP's capacity for M1 repolarization is evidenced by block at G6PDH, which was also evident in human M1-macrophages.
source: These data point to a block at G6PDH, which agreed with WGP's capacity for M1 repolarization as such block was also evident in human M1–MΦ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with M1 macrophage data.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP but not Pembrolizumab or WGP alone attenuated synthesis of 13C-glycogen and its precursors 13C6-G1P and -UDPG in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: Moreover, P + W but not Pembro or WGP treatment alone attenuated the synthesis of 13C-glycogen (i) and its precursors 13C6-G1P (g) and -UDPG (h) relative to the Ctl treatment (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5B.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP but not Pembrolizumab or WGP alone attenuated 13C incorporation into ribose and pyrimidine base of UTP in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: The P + W, but not Pembro or WGP treatment alone, attenuated the 13C incorporation into the ribose (5, d) and pyrimidine base (Base, d) of UTP, which reflected reduced synthesis of the respective 13C-precursors phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate PRPP (5, c) and Asp (a) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5C.

claim: Reduced UTP synthesis in Pembrolizumab + WGP-treated UK2035 CA OTC reflected reduced synthesis of precursors PRPP and Asp.
source: The P + W, but not Pembro or WGP treatment alone, attenuated the 13C incorporation into the ribose (5, d) and pyrimidine base (Base, d) of UTP, which reflected reduced synthesis of the respective 13C-precursors phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate PRPP (5, c) and Asp (a) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic tracing data.

claim: Disruption of the Krebs cycle and PPP at least in part accounted for decreased UTP synthesis in Pembrolizumab + WGP-treated UK2035 CA OTC.
source: Thus, disruption of the Krebs cycle and the PPP at least in part accounted for decreased UTP synthesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic data.

claim: Incorporation of 13C6-Glc-derived 13C-Gly and -ribose into ATP and GTP via purine nucleotide synthesis pathway was attenuated by Pembrolizumab + WGP but not by Pembrolizumab or WGP alone in UK2035 CA OTC.
source: Similarly, the incorporation of 13C6-Glc-derived 13C-Gly and -ribose into ATP (b) and GTP (c) via the purine nucleotide synthesis pathway was attenuated by P + W but not by Pembro or WGP alone (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5D.

claim: Reduced levels of 13Cbase and 13C5 isotopologues of ATP and GTP in Pembrolizumab + WGP-treated UK2035 CA OTC were opposite to buildup of corresponding isotopologues of precursor IMP.
source: This was shown by the reduced levels of both 13Cbase and 13C5 isotopologues of ATP and GTP in P + W-treated CA OTC. These were opposite to the buildup of the corresponding isotopologues of the precursor IMP (a), which points to a block downstream of IMP, possibly due to the reduced availability of the amino donor Asp (Figure 5C–a).
evidence: This is supported by metabolic tracing data in Figure 5D.

claim: Buildup of IMP isotopologues with depletion of ATP and GTP isotopologues points to a block downstream of IMP, possibly due to reduced availability of amino donor Asp.
source: This was shown by the reduced levels of both 13Cbase and 13C5 isotopologues of ATP and GTP in P + W-treated CA OTC. These were opposite to the buildup of the corresponding isotopologues of the precursor IMP (a), which points to a block downstream of IMP, possibly due to the reduced availability of the amino donor Asp (Figure 5C–a).
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolic data patterns.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP treatment inhibited energy and anabolic metabolism in metastatic NSCLC OTC, while Pembrolizumab or WGP treatment alone did not.
source: Altogether, P + W treatment inhibited energy and anabolic metabolism in metastatic NSCLC OTC, while Pembro or WGP treatment alone did not.
evidence: This is a summary inference from all the metabolic data in Figure 5.

claim: Results point to a synergistic interaction of Pembrolizumab and WGP in disrupting central metabolism in UK2035 tumor tissues.
source: These results point to a synergistic interaction of Pembro and WGP in disrupting central metabolism in UK2035 tumor tissues.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of combined versus single treatments.

claim: Pembrolizumab + WGP treatment was accompanied by increased release of proinflammatory effectors IL-6, INFα, IL-8, and MIP-1α by UK2035 CA OTC relative to control, Pembrolizumab, or WGP treatment.
source: The above metabolic disruptions induced by P + W treatment were accompanied by increased release of proinflammatory effectors IL-6, INFα, IL-8, and MIP-1α by CA OTC relative to Ctl, Pembro, or WGP treatment (Figure 6A–D).

claim: Although Pembrolizumab + WGP-induced cytokine changes in UK2035 CA OTC did not reach statistical significance, the trend points to M1-type polarization.
